title.narrative: Legal Resources Foundation Access to Justice 2020-2023
Legal Resources Foundation Access to Justice 2020-2023

description.narrative: Legal Resources Foundation har ansökt om 35 000 000 SEK som kärnstöd till Access to Justice Programme. Insatsmålen är följande: 1) Ökad tillgång till rättsskipning för marginaliserade och utsatta genom tillhandahållande av juridisk hjälp. 2) Att stärka marginaliserade och utsatta personers förmåga att hävda sina rättigheter genom tillhandahållande av information samt genom att utbilda samhällsadvokater och juridiska rådgivare som kan öka medvetenheten i lokala samhällen. 3) Bidra till en möjliggörande miljö där demokratiska rättigheter hävdas av en informerad allmänhet som kräver skydd och efterlevnad av konstitutionella och mänskliga rättigheter. 4) Ett effektivt och ansvarsfullt leveranssystem 5) Ökad tillgång till och förståelse för juridisk information.

The Legal Resources Foundation has applied for SEK 35 000 000, which is core support towards its Access to Justice Programme. The interventions objectives are as follows: 1) Increasing access to justice for the marginalized and vulnerable through the provision of legal assistance. 2) Strengthening the capacity of the marginalized and vulnerable to assert their rights through the provision of information as well as training community paralegals and peer legal advisors who can raise awareness in communities. 3) Contributing to an enabling environment where democratic rights are claimed by an informed public that demands the protection and enforcement of constitutional and human rights. 4) An efficient and accountable justice delivery system 5) Increased access to and understanding legal information.

description.narrative:
The below are the results achieved as at June 2024.
Increased access to justice for the marginalized and vulnerable (Legal Services)
3,042 new clients were assisted (1,506M:1 536F). LRF noted that the number of males reaching out for services increased in comparison to similar period last reflecting growing need for LRF services amongst men.
124 Mobile Legal Clinics reaching out to 1,287 people (1,009M:2,140F). Legal services were taken to remote rural areas enabling the most marginalised to access services. Areas which benefited include Karoi, Chipinge, Mutoko and Murambinda.
2, 862 cases resolved by paralegals through drafting of documents, legal advice, Alternative dispute resolution and referrals. This demonstrates the key role that paralegals have in enabling the marginalised to access justice in Zimbabwe 361 cases resolved by lawyers. The figures are on the lower side in comparison to similar period in 2023. This is due to the restructuring exercise which saw the LRF losing half of its center lawyers in April which resulting in fewer cases being attended to.
3,586 people assisted by LRF and presented their cases as self-actors in court. LRF empowered marginalised self-representing litigants to effectively table their cases before the courts. The assistance they received in preparing court process enabled the courts to quickly finalise the cases.
500 Help desk sessions conducted reaching out 2, 041 beneficiaries (1 276M:2 981F). 369 Call Centre beneficiaries assisted (121M; 248F). The call center enabled the LRF to assist marginalised beneficiaries remotely. They called from all Zimbabwe including Chivhu, Beitbridge, Binga and Chikomba districts. Beneficiaries were assisted through legal advice and referrals to key stakeholders including Registrar with some being invited to the LRF for further assistance.
Strengthened capacity of the marginalised and vulnerable to assert their rights. • 604 Community Volunteers, Human Rights Monitors, and Community Rights Resources persons advancing access to justice, human rights and service delivery in communities were capacitated during reporting period. They in turn conducted 1,238 sessions on legal information on birth certificates, citizenship, property rights, maintenance domestic violence amongst others.
13 Community dialogues provided platforms through which communities met with stakeholders which include members of Parliament, councillors, government departments and discussed pertinent issues affecting them with solutions being proffered and action being taken for development to take place. Issues discussed include service delivery, distribution of food id on partisan line, access to schools and health facilities , domestic violence and corporal punishment amongst others. 464 participants people participated (242F;222M)
124 Legal education sessions were conducted reaching out to 7 842 people (2 977M; 4 865F). The LRF enhanced the knowledge of different stakeholders for example on Birth Registration which strengthened coordination among the key stakeholders in Birth registration. This was achieved through the Access to documentation training workshops conducted in Districts like Mutoko and Karoi.
4 radio programme sessions were conducted during the period. The objectives of the radio programmes were to promote awareness of human rights and access to documentation in Zimbabwe. The programs covered various topics related to the birth registration process and the justice system on corruption. The programs reached a wide audience across 4 provinces, namely Masvingo, Manicaland, Midlands and Matabeleland. LRF made use of national and community four radio stations to ensure maximum reach of community members in hard-to-reach areas. Below is a table showing the estimated reach as shared by the radio stations.
During the period under review, LRF significantly expanded its social media reach and engagement. On Facebook, the organization shared 141 posts that reached an audience of 173,623 people. Of this audience, 16,468 were organic, while 151,722 were reached through advertising. The content generated 11,500 interactions, and the page's followers grew to 10,600 from 7967. The Face book page also saw a 282.2% increase in messaging conversations, with 187 out of 199 being new contacts, and the LRF maintained an 92% response rate to inquiries.
On YouTube, the LRF shared 7 videos that resulted in a total of 22,000 views and 619.8 hours of watch time. This content also helped the page increase its subscriber base from 1120 to 1437.
The LRF's Twitter presence was also impactful, with 329 tweets reaching an audience of 195,654 and generating 2,813 likes, 807 re-tweets, 89 new followers, 409 profile visits, and 183 comments.
Additionally, the LRF shared 34 sets of bulk SMS messages to 1,090 people, further expanding its reach and engagement.
The LRF website experienced a significant influx of traffic, with approximately 8,252 visits recorded. The most popular sections were the Board (3,470 views), LRF Home (1,109 visits), and LRF press statements (1,089 visits), demonstrating a keen interest in the organization's leadership, governance, and public communications.
The legal services section received 596 visits, showcasing the demand for the organization's expertise in legal matters. The contact section was accessed by 495 people, suggesting that users were seeking to engage with the LRF directly.
You tube- during the second quarter, the channel accumulated a total of 11,340 views, showcasing a consistent level of interest from viewers. Two videos were posted on the page. The watch time reached 329.9 hours, indicating that the audience was not only clicking on the videos but also spending a significant amount of time watching them. In terms of impressions, the channel achieved 27,493, demonstrating that the content was being widely seen. The most popular video was on the topic of Property Rights, which garnered 521 views. This indicates a strong interest in this subject matter, providing valuable insight for future content planning.
The demographic breakdown revealed that the audience was predominantly male, with 83.3% male viewers and 16.7% female viewers. This information is important in noting the gap in uptake of information on social media between males and females as females could access information on the form of pamphlets.
The website views continue to steadily increase with the home page fetching the highest views of 15 457 views, while the Contact Us fetched 1 936 page views, followed by the legal services section with 1547 views, and the About Us Section with 1167 viewership, while the Board section fetched 472.
